Verify rewrite DATA ONLY. Do not write improved examples or solve the user's task.
Read every input and target in full. Return one review per exact id and row_sha256.
input_verdict checks plausible natural drafts or dictation, recoverable intent, contradictions,
fake noise, padding and leaked authoring instructions. output_verdict checks natural appropriate
language and formatting. pair_verdict checks ALL facts, uncertainty, conditions, negation,
quantities, names, quotations, literals, requests versus assertions, and the supplied mode.
/transcribe permits punctuation, true disfluency removal and explicit corrections, not lexical
paraphrasing. Preserve meaningful words like German 'um' and 'er', colloquial Portuguese and
unfinished thoughts. /slack is casual minimal cleanup; a long input may be a pasted thread.
/prompt reorganizes a self-contained request and never answers it. It must not drop supplied
material, hedges or constraints. /polish improves prose without omissions or changed certainty.
Identity inputs must remain byte-identical. Apply only supplied dictionary/profile context.
Check long texts paragraph by paragraph. Fail concrete defects. Uncertain means not confidently
justifiable. Pass requires no material defect. Overall verdict is fail if any dimension fails,
uncertain if any dimension is uncertain and none fails, otherwise pass. Give a concrete critique
for EVERY pair, citing the changed detail for defects. These are model judgments, not human labels.

[{"id": "arka-boost-prompt-long-0035", "row_sha256": "9e348ce417f41c4be61ab7b3b0851366830680a80535e6541695e6749d7612a6", "mode": "/prompt", "language": "en", "context": {}, "identity": false, "mode_instructions": "Organize the supplied request into a clear prompt. Preserve scope and constraints. Do not invent context, requirements, or missing information. Do not perform the task.", "input": "i need a good prompt for a ventilation check at north quay repair workshop, not a report that says the check already happened. we are getting ready for a visit planned for 16 may, 9 to 11 in the morning. Noor Patel is leading and Eli Morgan is accompanying as an apprentice. the shop runs monday to friday, 7:00 to 3:30, and usually has five people working. the visit is supposed to look at the ventilation arrangements and give us a useful way to record what is actually seen. please turn all this into a clear request for an assistant to draft a visit sheet and a short handoff note. don't have the assistant invent readings or state a result.

there are several bits of the shop to keep straight. the welding area is at the east bench, and the local exhaust there is called E-2. the ceiling supply fan is GF-1 and serves the general workshop space. the roller door is on the south side and the personnel entrance is on the west side. there's also a paint-preparation corner on the north wall. don't imply that there is a separate exhaust system in that corner because i haven't given you that. E-2 is the one unit with the recent service note below. the check should allow Noor to note whether the systems and openings are being used in their normal arrangement, but the visit is an observation and recording exercise, not permission to take anything apart or change a setting. staff can explain their routine, but the prompt shouldn't tell the visitors to operate equipment or adjust it.

we have heard a few different things and they need to stay as reports from people, not become established findings. one welder said, “the east bench is still dusty by lunch”. a second person said, “we open the roller door when the welding bay gets hot”. someone else said, “the extractor sounds different after the belt was changed”. keep those exact words and make clear the comments are attributed reports. the request could have a place to record who said something and when, if known, without supplying a name or time we don't have. none of these remarks proves that the ventilation works or doesn't work. don't rewrite them into technical conclusions.

these are the short records to use as supplied; please include them in the prompt word for word, not replace them with a reference to source notes. Work order VC-184, opened 12 May; requested check: local exhaust and general air movement. Prior service entry, 6 May: belt replaced on unit E-2; no post-change airflow figure recorded. Room log, 13 May, 08:10: outdoor temperature 4 °C; roller door closed. the room-log entry is from another day, so it isn't a measurement for the planned visit. the notes don't say who made the service entry or who wrote the room log, and we should not fill that in.

for a useful sheet, ask for a simple sequence that Noor and Eli can follow without turning this into a broad engineering assessment. it can start with visit details and a short preparation part, then have a walk-through record by location or system: east bench/E-2, general space/GF-1, south roller door, west personnel entrance, and north paint-preparation corner. for each, give a place for observed condition or use, the time, and any context that affects the observation. a blank field is better than a guessed value. include room for a short description of what was visible or audible, but distinguish that from a person's account. don't require a particular measurement, since no instrument, method, or readings have been supplied. if the sheet includes readings as optional entries, leave them empty and make it clear they are only filled if actually taken.

include the door issue as something to record carefully. if the outdoor temperature at the visit is below 5 °C, the sheet should ask the visitors to record the temperature and whether the roller door is open or closed; when it is closed, don't present that one visit as representative of typical operation. the room log says 4 °C on 13 May with the door closed, but that doesn't tell us the temperature or door position on 16 May. keep that conditional instruction in the eventual prompt so it can't get lost in a general weather field. also distinguish the planned two-hour visit window from the workshop's full shift; don't imply the visitors saw the whole day's operation.

please have the requested assistant output a practical visit sheet and a brief handoff note, with a numbered section in the sheet for the walk-through locations. the handoff can identify what was observed, what was reported by staff, and what remains unknown, but it should be a place to summarize evidence rather than a conclusion about performance. use the exact names and equipment labels above. include the three spoken comments and all three record lines exactly as supplied. the sheet should leave space for the visit date and actual times, names present, door position, weather, and any follow-up question that still needs an answer. if an item was not checked, allow it to be marked not checked instead of implying that it was checked. keep the request focused on this workshop, the upcoming visit, and the information given here; don't add legal standards, pass/fail thresholds, diagnoses, repairs, or a recommendation that has already been agreed. the final paragraph of the prompt should make clear that this is a preparation tool for the 16 May visit, that no visit findings are available yet, and that the assistant is being asked to create the sheet and handoff template rather than fill them in.", "output": "Draft a practical visit sheet and a brief handoff-note template for the planned ventilation check at North Quay Repair Workshop on 16 May, 9:00–11:00 a.m. Noor Patel is leading the visit, accompanied by Eli Morgan, an apprentice. The workshop operates Monday to Friday from 7:00 a.m. to 3:30 p.m. and usually has five people working. Create preparation materials only: do not write a completed report, invent readings, or state a result.

### Purpose and scope

The visit is an observation and recording exercise focused on the workshop’s ventilation arrangements. Do not present it as a broad engineering assessment, and do not imply permission to dismantle equipment, operate it, or change any settings. Staff may explain their routine; the visitors should not be instructed to operate equipment or adjust it. Distinguish what the visitors observe from what people report. Do not add legal standards, pass/fail thresholds, diagnoses, repairs, or agreed recommendations.

Use the supplied locations and equipment labels:
- East welding bench: local exhaust unit E-2.
- General workshop space: ceiling supply fan GF-1.
- South side: roller door.
- West side: personnel entrance.
- North wall: paint-preparation corner. No separate exhaust system for this corner has been specified; do not imply that one exists.

### Supplied remarks and records

Keep each staff comment exactly as written and identify it as a reported remark, not an established finding. Provide space to record who said it and when, if known, without filling in missing details.

- A welder said, “the east bench is still dusty by lunch”.
- A second person said, “we open the roller door when the welding bay gets hot”.
- Someone else said, “the extractor sounds different after the belt was changed”.

These remarks do not establish whether the ventilation works or does not work. Do not recast them as technical conclusions.

Include the following records word for word:

Work order VC-184, opened 12 May; requested check: local exhaust and general air movement.

Prior service entry, 6 May: belt replaced on unit E-2; no post-change airflow figure recorded.

Room log, 13 May, 08:10: outdoor temperature 4 °C; roller door closed.

The room-log entry is from another day and is not a measurement for the planned visit. The records do not identify who made the service entry or room-log entry; leave those details unspecified.

### Visit sheet

Organize the sheet as a simple sequence that Noor and Eli can use. Begin with visit details and brief preparation notes, then provide a numbered walk-through section. Include these locations in that section:

1. East bench / E-2
2. General workshop space / GF-1
3. South roller door
4. West personnel entrance
5. North paint-preparation corner

For each location, provide space to note the observed condition or use, the time, and relevant context. Include room for a short description of what was visible or audible, clearly separate from any account given by a person. Allow an item to be marked “not checked” rather than implying that it was checked. Do not require a particular measurement: no instrument, method, or readings have been supplied. Optional reading fields, if included, must remain blank until an actual reading is taken.

Provide space for the visit date and actual times, people present, weather, roller-door position, and follow-up questions that remain unanswered. Keep the planned two-hour window distinct from the workshop’s full shift; do not imply that the visitors observed the whole day’s operation.

If the outdoor temperature during the visit is below 5 °C, the sheet must prompt the visitors to record the temperature and whether the roller door is open or closed. If it is closed, do not present that single visit as representative of typical operation. The 13 May room-log entry does not establish the temperature or door position on 16 May. Preserve this conditional instruction rather than reducing it to a general weather field.

### Handoff note

Provide a brief template that separates what was observed, what staff reported, and what remains unknown. It should summarize evidence, not reach a conclusion about ventilation performance. Leave space for any follow-up question still needing an answer, without adding an agreed recommendation.

This is a preparation tool for the 16 May visit; no visit findings are available yet. Create the visit sheet and handoff template only, and do not fill them in."}]
